2.8.55.en: St. John Chrysostom * The adversary tempted Job through his sons and possessions (Job 1:13), and since he could not conquer him he brought his equipment, coming with him the daughter of Eve who overwhelmed Adam, and through her mouth he said to Job, the righteous husband: [Curse God], but Job refused the counsel.

2.8.56.en: King Asa also triumphed over the sodomites of the land when (Satan) came to him to fight him through his mother (1 Kgs 15:12-13). Asa knew his cunning, and removed his mother from her high position (queen), and cut down her image and cast it away.

2.8.57.en: John was greater than all the prophets, but Herod slew him because of the dance of the daughter of Eve (Mt 11:11, 14; etc.).

2.8.58.en: Haman was rich, third in honor from the king, but his wife advised him to kill the Jews (Esth 6:13).

2.8.59.en: Zimri was head of the tribe of Simeon, but Cozbi the daughter of the head of the tribes of Midian cast him down, and because of one woman twenty-four thousand persons of Israel fell in one day (Num 25:6-15).

2.8.60.en: St. Aphrahat “And he said unto her: Thou speakest as one of the foolish women speaketh!

2.8.61.en: What? shall we receive good at the hand of God, and shall we not receive evil?

2.9.0.en: In all this did not Job sin with his lips” [10].

2.9.1.en: * Job in the hours of his grief was more watchful than Adam on the throne of his happiness.

2.9.2.en: One was defeated amid pleasures, and the other conquered amid sufferings.

2.9.3.en: One agreed to what seemed pleasant, and the other did not wither amid pains of the utmost terror...

2.9.4.en: He bore his pain in his body, and bore in his heart the faults of others, rebuking his wife for her folly, teaching his companions wisdom, keeping patience in all circumstances.

2.9.5.en: St. Augustine * Note, beloved brethren, that he never said: “This is the work of Satan.”

2.9.6.en: Ascribe the chastening directly to your God, for Satan does nothing without the permission of Him who governs your affairs by the power of His authority, whether for punishment or for teaching; for punishment as regards the wicked and for teaching as regards the son. For He “scourgeth every son whom he receiveth” (Heb 12:6).

2.9.7.en: You need not flee from the rod, unless you do not wish to inherit.

2.9.8.en: * When his body was covered with sores his wife came to him, who had been left to him as another Eve, to be Satan's companion instead of being a helper to her husband. She was constantly rebuking him sharply to shake his loyalty, saying: [Say a word against God, and die].

2.9.9.en: But the Adam on the dunghill was wiser than the Adam who was in Paradise.

2.9.10.en: Adam in Paradise gave his ear to the woman, so that they were driven out of Paradise. And Adam on the dunghill cast the woman aside only that they might enter Paradise.

2.9.11.en: And what did the Adam on the dunghill have? Inwardly he was begetting immortality; outwardly he was food for worms.

2.9.12.en: What did he say to his wife? “Thou speakest as one of the foolish women speaketh. What? shall we receive good at the hand of God, and shall we not receive evil?” (Job 2:10).

2.9.13.en: He repeats that God's hand was upon him when Satan was striking, for he did not look to the one who aimed the blow at him, but to the One who gave him the authority.

2.9.14.en: For Satan himself in turn called that authority which he begged from the hand of the Lord.

2.9.15.en: St. Augustine * I choose that the Lord visit my sins and correct my transgressions here in this world, so that Abraham may say to me there what he said about poor Lazarus in his conversation with the rich man: “Son, remember that thou in thy lifetime receivedst thy good things, and likewise Lazarus evil things: but now he is comforted, and thou art tormented” (Lk 16:25).

2.9.16.en: For this reason, when the Lord rebukes us, when He chastens us, we must not be ungrateful.

2.9.17.en: Let us realize, then, that our being rebuked in the present time is so that we may receive comfort in the future. As the Apostle says: “But when we are judged, we are chastened of the Lord, that we should not be condemned with the world” (1 Cor 11:32). For this reason Job also accepted all his sufferings willingly, saying: “What? shall we receive good at the hand of God, and shall we not receive evil?”

2.9.18.en: Origen * He became more blessed than anyone, for not only did he do nothing to cause him to stumble, but he practiced what made him more steadfast. His wife troubled him along with all these, and yet he shone in everything.

2.9.19.en: * A wife is a great good, just as she can also be a grave evil. For the wife is great; note from what point Satan wanted to enter through the strong wall.

2.9.20.en: St. John Chrysostom The Septuagint reads: [But he looked at her and said to her: Thou speakest as one of the foolish women] (Job 2:10).

2.9.21.en: * Meaning: You are not speaking what befits you, nor your teaching, nor the formation you received from me.

2.9.22.en: These words do not befit you.

2.9.23.en: He did not wish to rebuke her violently, but to turn her back from this corrupt thinking.

2.9.24.en: “If we receive good things from the hand of God, shall we not endure evils?” Meaning, if indeed these things are nothing but evils, let us bear them.

2.9.25.en: He is the Lord and Master; does He not have authority over everything He sends upon us?

2.9.26.en: Why did He give us good things? Not out of any merit on our part.

2.9.27.en: May we not be anxious from this day on by thinking that we suffer undeservedly.

2.9.28.en: He is completely free, even if He gave us only evils.

2.9.29.en: If He gives us good things also, why should we complain?

2.9.30.en: Note that he never spoke of transgressions, nor of good works, but spoke only of God, who has the authority to do what He wills.

2.9.31.en: Remember your former good things and you will not find it hard to bear the present troubles. It is enough for us, for our consolation, to realize that the Lord has sent them to us. Do not speak of justice or injustice.

2.9.32.en: St. John Chrysostom *“He looked at her” (Job 2:10) LXX, he looked at his wife, in order to discern the one who was speaking in her, and to be on guard against the serpent hidden in his wife's speech.

2.9.33.en: * Shall we not offer our patience as an acceptable sacrifice (Rom 12:1), through which we recover what we lost, and receive other blessings greater than they?

2.9.34.en: * “In all this did not Job sin with his lips.” Did God deliver Job to this struggle in vain? Did He not truly know His fighter? Does the King not know His soldier...?

2.9.35.en: As for us, let us imitate his patience. Let us fight with gentleness, let us practice his patience, and equal him in his trust in God.

2.9.36.en: Let us be formed according to his faith without failure, and let us be steadfast in his spirit, in the truth of his words, in his struggle with an unseen enemy, in his solitude, and in his trials, in his calmness, in facing all that arises, that we may remain strong and firm of resolve.

2.9.37.en: In all sufferings let us be godly and complete our testing. For by this we share in the crowns, and become partners in his victory, and God will be the witness of our righteousness. To Him be glory forever. Amen.

2.9.38.en: Fr. Hesychius of Jerusalem * Let the Almighty be summoned to your aid against the wiles of Satan.

2.9.39.en: Let Him dwell in you, He who cannot be conquered, for you will surely overcome the one who was accustomed to conquer. But whom does he conquer? Those in whom God does not dwell.

2.9.40.en: For you, brethren, know this, that Adam in Paradise despised the commandment of God, and lifted up his neck, like one who wanted to be master of himself, and shrank from submitting to God's will. Thus he fell from immortality and blessedness.

2.9.41.en: But a man was found, a brilliant proven one, though mortal by birth, and though he sat on a dunghill and was corrupt with worms, he conquered Satan.

2.9.42.en: Yes, Adam himself has prevailed even in Job, because Job is of his race.

2.9.43.en: Adam was defeated in Paradise, and was overcome on the dunghill.

2.9.44.en: Being in Paradise, he lent his ear to the persuasion of the woman into whom Satan had entered, but when on the dunghill he said to Eve: “Thou speakest as one of the foolish women.”

2.9.45.en: There he lent her his ear; here he gave her an answer.

2.9.46.en: When he was happy he listened, and when he was afflicted he conquered.

2.9.47.en: Therefore see what followed this, my brethren, in the Epistle (1 Jn 2:9). For this is what we must put in our hearts, that we truly conquer Satan, but not by ourselves, for he says: “If ye know that he is righteous, ye know that every one that doeth righteousness is born of him.”

2.9.48.en: St. Augustine * It is written: “a man's foes shall be they of his own household” (Mt 10:36), for when the crafty adversary sees that he has withdrawn from the hearts of the good, he seeks out those who are most beloved by them, and speaks to them sweetly with words most dear to them, so that when the power of love steals into the heart the sword of his persuasion can easily break through to the inner defenses of the righteous.

2.9.49.en: * By good here is meant either the temporal or the eternal gifts of God, and by evil the blows of the present time, those about which the Lord said through the prophet: “I am the LORD, and there is none else, I form the light, and create darkness: I make peace, and create evil.” (Isa 45:6-7) He does not mean the evil which has no substance by nature as being created by God. Rather, the Lord Himself is reckoned the creator of evil (affliction) when He turns evil into punishment (or discipline), so that these things are evil for the disobedient in their bearing of pain, and at the same time good by nature...

2.9.50.en: It is a mighty comfort for our trials, when we bear sorrows and remember our Creator's gifts to us... For it is said: [In the day of good things do not forget afflictions, and in the day of afflictions do not forget good things] (Sir 11:27).

2.9.51.en: For he who receives God's gifts in the season of gifts and does not fear the blows falls by his joy into wandering of mind, and he who suffers punishments, and yet in the season of punishments ignores his comfort in the gifts he had received, falls from the steadiness of his mind into despair on every side.

2.9.53.en: His wife mocked him for his simplicity and his attachment to eternal things, and she counted this simplicity as folly and ignorance and deprivation of life and happiness. Therefore she saw his death as far better than his life, and blaspheming God as more fitting than worshiping Him while suffering pains.

2.9.54.en: * It is as though he says: If we incline toward eternal blessings, what wonder if we face temporal evils? Paul fixed his eyes on these blessings with great attention when he submitted his mind to the evils that befell him. He says: “For I reckon that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which shall be revealed in us” (Rom 8:18).

2.9.56.en: Job did not sin with his mouth, for he did not utter a word that did not befit him as a believer. St. Peter the Apostle warns us against sinning with the mouth, saying: [Let none of you suffer as a murderer, or a thief, or one who speaks evil] (1 Pet 4:15) Vulgate.

2.10.0.en: 11 Now when Job's three friends heard of all this evil that was come upon him, they came every one from his own place; Eliphaz the Temanite, and Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite: for they had made an appointment together to come to mourn with him and to comfort him. 12 And when they lifted up their eyes afar off, and knew him not, they lifted up their voice, and wept; and they rent every one his mantle, and sprinkled dust upon their heads toward heaven. 13 So they sat down with him upon the ground seven days and seven nights, and none spake a word unto him: for they saw that his grief was very great.

2.10.1.en: “Now when Job's three friends heard of all this evil that was come upon him, they came every one from his own place;

2.10.2.en: Eliphaz the Temanite, and Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite: for they had made an appointment together to come to mourn with him and to comfort him” [11].

2.10.3.en: Here he mentioned the names of his three friends who came to sympathize with him and comfort him. Perhaps the young man Elihu was present with them, and he listened to the discussions, and it seems he was not a friend of Job because he was much younger than he, but he attended as a listener. Perhaps he loved to sit with elders, and perhaps the sight of Job in his tragedy attracted him, so that he longed to offer him some service or a word of consolation.

2.10.4.en: As for the three friends, they were advanced in age, indeed they were elders, famed for knowledge, wisdom and goodness, and they were esteemed, and their opinions were met with respect (Job 32:6). Perhaps they held high positions in the state, as princes or chiefs. Perhaps they were his relatives, for the three were descendants of Abraham, and most likely they inherited from him some teachings and good fruits. Eliphaz the Temanite, king of Teman, was the son of Teman, the grandson of Esau (Gen 36:11). Some see that Eliphaz here is not the eldest son of Esau but his grandson who was called by his name. Bildad the Shuhite was the son of Shuah, whom Keturah bore to Abraham (Gen 25:2). And Zophar the Naamathite is supposed to be Zepho, the grandson of Esau (Gen 36:11). All three were of the Gentiles, and bore some good traits, among them that, unlike most of the friends, they did not leave Job in his trial, but came to share his sorrows as they had shared before in his joys.

2.10.5.en: They came not out of curiosity, nor at anyone's invitation, but agreed together in doing good. They were sincere in their desire to comfort, though it became clear that they were wearisome comforters because of their lack of wisdom in handling the matter.

2.10.6.en: We did not hear that any of the poor and needy whom he supported, nor of the orphans and widows whom he cared for, came to ask about him in his trial. Perhaps they heard of the successive calamities and fell into what these three friends fell into, and reckoned that he was a wicked man who had hidden his wickedness with outward gifts and showy concern.

2.10.7.en: The absence of any of them undoubtedly had its bad effect on Job's spirit, since he reckoned that they had stumbled over his person.

2.11.0.en: “And when they lifted up their eyes afar off, and knew him not, they lifted up their voice, and wept; and they rent every one his mantle, and sprinkled dust upon their heads toward heaven” [12].

2.11.1.en: Grief and bitterness often disfigure a person's appearance, so that his elder friends did not recognize him, because his sores deformed his body, and the bitterness of his soul removed his cheerfulness from him. This is what happened with Naomi when grief disfigured her appearance, so that when she returned to her country the people of the city asked: “Is this Naomi?” (Ruth 1:19).

2.11.2.en: The elders could not contain themselves, so they lifted up their voices like children and wept, and each tore his mantle, and they sprinkled dust on their heads. And they sat with him on the ground. It was as though they shared his humiliation.

2.11.3.en: They did not meet him on the level of formal courtesies, but as loved ones sharing the bitterness of his soul. As partners in the severe affliction they could not open their mouths for seven days and seven nights; they were silent, astonished. The Latin proverb says: “Light sorrows speak, but heavy ones tie the tongue.”

2.11.4.en: At first they avoided speaking lest they add weight to his trial, and perhaps because they wanted to take time so that each might examine this baffling riddle, for they knew the works of his great love to which all bore witness, but was there some hidden sin that caused him all these disasters? Does God wish to reveal to him what he had hidden in his heart and mind, or works that no one knows?

2.11.5.en: * Job's friends did not recognize him, for they did not see the purple robe nor the high throne, nor the royal crown and the soldiers in service, nor the servants at their tasks. Instead of the throne he had the hard ground, the dunghill instead of a bed, and instead of a house the open air.

2.12.0.en: Fr. Hesychius of Jerusalem “So they sat down with him upon the ground seven days and seven nights, and none spake a word unto him: for they saw that his grief was very great” [13].

2.12.1.en: They had agreed to come and meet together at Job's, but what astonishes us is that they remained silent seven days and seven nights without uttering a word, and when they spoke they attacked him with great violence, as with one opinion.

2.12.2.en: They showed at first exaggerated grief, followed by quarreling and bitter arguments amid his pains.

2.12.3.en: What love was this that moved them to agree together and sit around him amid the unbearable stench for a whole week? And why the sudden change, to the exact opposite?

2.12.4.en: Were they perhaps sincere in their love for him, but offered a love without discernment? Or was the intention evil, hidden under the guise of intense grief, so that what was inside them burst out?

2.12.5.en: Pope Gregory (the Great) sees that these friends are a type of the heretics, who at first show excessive tenderness, and though sincere in intention to act, lack the spirit of discernment. Therefore Job says to them: “But ye are forgers of lies, ye are all physicians of no value” (Job 13:3-4).

2.12.6.en: They came every one from his own place (Job 2:11), and the place of the heretics is pride itself. They came by appointment in agreement under the guise of love and friendship.

2.12.7.en: Thus heretics often agree together against the Church of God, and bear the appearance of friendship and service and conduct in virtue.

2.12.8.en: Finally God asked them to ask Job to pray for them, and to offer a sacrifice for them; thus the Church does not cease to pray for the heretics that they may turn from resistance, and recover their membership in the Church, and enjoy the heavenly life of the Church.

2.12.9.en: * All these gestures are good and fitting for friends who reveal their sympathy with him, but what came afterwards was the opposite. It was not of the same kind, but quite the opposite and wicked. See what happened. It is unbelievable, they spoke as spiteful adversaries.

2.12.10.en: * When the soul is filled with despair immediately it is not inclined to hear anything of what is said. Therefore when Job's friends came and saw the catastrophe of his house, and the righteous man sitting in the mire, covered with sores, they tore their garments and sighed, and sat beside him in silence, showing that nothing is fitting to offer one who suffers thus but quiet and stillness. For the trial was far greater than to have a consolation.

2.12.13.en: * Satan could not keep silent when he saw man in the garden of Eden enjoying You as his Paradise!

2.12.14.en: He approached him through the serpent, and dared to use the mouth of Eve.

2.12.15.en: And by his envy he drove Adam and Eve out of the garden, and by sin death reigned over them and over their offspring!

2.12.16.en: * Now that he has seen in every person the broken Adam.

2.12.17.en: He thought he could break Job as he broke his first father.

2.12.18.en: He did not speak with him through the serpent, but dared to accuse him before You, O Creator of all!

2.12.19.en: * In pride he declared that he was going about the earth and walking upon it, as though he were a king with authority!

2.12.20.en: Yes, remove our dust from us, that we may no longer remain earth, and he may not be able to walk about in our hearts!

2.12.21.en: He will see us as a second heaven, and will flee from before us.

2.12.22.en: You make us sit in the heavenly places, so he cannot creep in to us!

2.12.23.en: * How wonderful, You alone, the Holy One, praise us!

2.12.24.en: And the evil devil accuses us!

2.12.25.en: Is he jealous for holiness, that he accuses us of our weakness?

2.12.26.en: In his wickedness he wishes to destroy all, that they may share with him his blasphemy against You, O You who alone are holy!

2.12.27.en: * He aimed all his fiery darts at poor Job!

2.12.28.en: He who was the morning star stands before an unarmed man!

2.12.29.en: He had no rest until he struck his whole body!

2.12.30.en: With Your permission he killed all his sons and daughters, and left his wife to use against him.

2.12.31.en: He struck his whole body, and left him his tongue in the hope that he might blaspheme You!

2.12.32.en: With great cunning he spent all his effort to break the one who believes in You, and did not realize that his arrows turn back upon him!

2.12.33.en: * Adam in the garden inclined his ear to hear the enemy's counsel, through Eve his helper!

2.12.34.en: Job in the midst of the ashes opened his mouth to silence the satanic counsel!

2.12.35.en: Adam was silent with a sinful silence, and broke Your divine commandment.

2.12.36.en: And Job spoke good words, and rescued his wife from the satanic wiles!

2.12.37.en: Adam was stripped bare in the garden, and fig leaves could not cover him!

2.12.38.en: And Job put on a garment of worms, more splendidly beautiful than the garment of kings!

2.12.39.en: Adam and Eve were terrified when they heard Your voice!

2.12.40.en: And the heavenly ones stood in amazement before the praises of the one sitting in the midst of the ashes!

2.12.41.en: Adam supposed that his being forbidden to eat of the tree of knowledge was injustice and deprivation.

2.12.42.en: And Job reckoned that all that was taken from him was by Your permission for his good!

2.12.43.en: Amid all the blessings of the garden and its possibilities Adam's eyes were fixed on one tree!

2.12.44.en: Amid all the unbearable trials Job's eyes were fixed on You, O Maker of good things!

2.12.45.en: Adam opened his mouth to justify himself, and Job opened his mouth and did not sin with his lips!

2.12.46.en: * The friends came, each from his own place, and would that they had not come!

2.12.47.en: They wanted to comfort him with their human thoughts, and gave him bitterness!

2.12.48.en: They showed all feelings of tenderness and sharing in the sufferings, but they did not bring You to him, O heavenly Comforter!

2.12.49.en: * You are my heavenly Friend, carry me to You, to Your place, that I may rest in the bosom of Your Father!

2.12.50.en: You came down to me, and were tempted that You might help those who are tempted!

2.12.51.en: Be You the secret of my comfort, my peace and my true joy!
